title: Anansi and the Pot of Wisdom
text:
In the stories of the Ashanti people of Ghana, Anansi the spider once gathered up all the wisdom in the world and sealed it in a pot. Now he would be the wisest of all creatures, and everyone would have to come to him for advice.

But he worried that someone might steal it. He decided to hide the pot at the top of a very tall tree, where no one could reach it. He tied the pot to the front of his body and began to climb. The pot hung between him and the trunk, bumping against the bark, and every time he tried to pull himself up, it got in his way. He slipped and tried again and slipped again.

His young son Ntikuma had been watching from the ground. Father, he called up, why not tie the pot on your back? Then you could hold the tree.

Anansi was furious. He had all the wisdom of the world in his pot, and a small child had seen what he had missed. In his anger he let the pot fall. It smashed on the ground, and the wisdom scattered in every direction. People came from everywhere and picked up pieces of it, and that is why wisdom is shared among everyone today.
lesson: Nobody holds all the good ideas, and keeping knowledge to yourself makes you less wise, not more. Listen to the person you least expect to help.
caveat: Versions differ on details, such as whether the pot belonged to the sky god Nyame.
